title: t6: counting the tokens that share the last token's class (mlp0 -> head 1.1 -> mlp1)
label: verified
behavior: Input BOS + 6 tokens from {do, ge, go, ko, no, vu}; at the last position the model outputs a digit. Backend: local-full (full precision) for every number in this report.
summary: The model outputs how many of the 6 input tokens belong to the same class as the last token (the last token counts itself), with classes {do,vu}, {ge,no}, {go,ko} (token ids {2,7}, {3,6}, {4,5}). The rule was read off the dataset examples and reproduces the model on 200/200 held-out inputs. The circuit is three components: mlp0 (acts per token at every input position), head 1.1 (from the last position attends uniformly over BOS plus all same-class tokens, so BOS weight = 1/(1+count)), and mlp1 (acts only at the last position and turns that into the digit). Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 and 1.2 play no part: ablating all five together changes nothing.
pseudocode:
cls = {do:0, vu:0, ge:1, no:1, go:2, ko:2}
# mlp0, at each input position: token -> class feature
# head 1.1, at the last position: attend uniformly to BOS + tokens with cls == cls[last]  -> BOS weight 1/(1+count)
# mlp1, at the last position: 1/(1+count) -> digit
count = sum(cls[t] == cls[tokens[-1]] for t in tokens[1:])
return digit(count)   # id 8 + count

claims.text: The model performs its behaviour deterministically (accuracy 1.0 on 128 inputs).
The function is: number of input tokens in the last token's class, classes {2,7},{3,6},{4,5}; the coded rule agrees with the model on 200/200 held-out inputs (task-shuffled null max 0.315).
Head 1.1 is necessary: mean-ablating it leaves 0.0 of the clean metric.
mlp0 and mlp1 are both necessary: mean-ablating either leaves 0.0 and 0.012 of the clean metric.
Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0, 1.2 play no part: joint mean ablation leaves the metric at 1.0, and the circuit alone (everything else ablated) keeps accuracy 1.0.

Head 1.1 at the last position attends uniformly over BOS plus same-class tokens (matching on class, not identity): BOS weight is 1/7 when all six tokens are class-mates of mixed identity, and 1/2 (self 1/2, all others 0) when the last token is alone in its class.

mlp1 does its work only at the last position (patching its output there alone restores the full answer; other positions 0), while mlp0 works at every input position 1-6 (single-position patches give partial effects 0.25-0.43, BOS 0).
Ablating the circuit {mlp0, 1.1, mlp1} drops the metric to 0.0085 of clean (accuracy 0.35); random same-size sets leave it at 1.0.

edges.label: class (inferred from layer order; not path-patched)

limitations: The mlp0 -> 1.1 edge is inferred from layer order, necessity and per-position patching; path_patching with an MLP sender raised an error, so it was not measured whether mlp0 feeds 1.1's query, key or both.
That mlp0 writes a 'class' feature is an interpretation consistent with 1.1's class-matching attention; the feature itself was not probed.
That mlp1 reads 1/(1+count) is inferred from the attention pattern; the value 1.1 moves was not decoded directly.
E0008 was scored inconclusive because of a wrong metric path (observed 1.0); it was re-run on a fresh seed with the same threshold as E0012.
Exploratory E0014 shows heads 1.0 and 1.2 have nonzero direct writes along the answer direction (0.21, 0.19) although ablating them does not change the output.
open_questions: Does mlp0 feed head 1.1 through the query, the key, or both?
What do the unused heads 1.0 and 1.2 write, given their nonzero direct logit attribution?
